knowledge_point.title: Writing First-Order Linear ODEs in Standard Form

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
2 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 3 \cos{(x )}=- 4 y \sin{(x )} + 1\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}2 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 3 \cos{(x )}=- 4 y \sin{(x )} + 1 \\ 2 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 4 y \sin{(x )}=3 \cos{(x )} + 1 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(2 \sin{(x )})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{\frac{3 \cos{(x )}}{2} + \frac{1}{2}}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=2 \sin{(x )}$ and $Q(x)=\frac{3 \cos{(x )}}{2} + \frac{1}{2}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
2 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + \cos{(x )}=y \sin{(x )} - 1\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}2 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + \cos{(x )}=y \sin{(x )} - 1 \\ 2 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - y \sin{(x )}=- \cos{(x )} - 1 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- \frac{\sin{(x )}}{2})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{- \frac{\cos{(x )}}{2} - \frac{1}{2}}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- \frac{\sin{(x )}}{2}$ and $Q(x)=- \frac{\cos{(x )}}{2} - \frac{1}{2}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2 x - y}{x}\,.
$$

Assume $x\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2 x - y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2 x}{x}-\frac{y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + \frac{y}{x}=\frac{2 x}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(\frac{1}{x})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{2}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=\frac{1}{x}$ and $Q(x)=2.$

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{- x + y}{x}\,.
$$

Assume $x\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{- x + y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{- x}{x}+\frac{y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - \frac{y}{x}=\frac{- x}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- \frac{1}{x})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{-1}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} e^{2 x} - x + 2 y e^{x}=0\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} e^{2 x} - x + 2 y e^{x}=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} e^{2 x} + 2 y e^{x}=x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(2 e^{- x})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{x e^{- 2 x}}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=2 e^{- x}$ and $Q(x)=x e^{- 2 x}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \cos{(x )} - y \sin{(x )} + \sin{(2 x )}=0\,.
$$

Assume $\cos{(x )}\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \cos{(x )} - y \sin{(x )} + \sin{(2 x )}=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \cos{(x )} - y \sin{(x )}=- \sin{(2 x )} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - \frac{y \sin{(x )}}{\cos{(x )}}=- \frac{\sin{(2 x )}}{\cos{(x )}} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - y \tan{(x )}=\frac{- 2 \sin{(x )}\cos{(x )}}{\cos{(x )}} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- \tan{(x )})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{- 2 \sin{(x )}}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- \tan{(x )}$ and $Q(x)=- 2 \sin{(x )}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y + x^{2} y=x y^{2}\,.
$$

Assume $y\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y + x^{2} y=x y^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y + x^{2} y - x y^{2}=0 \\ y (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + x^{2} - x y)=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + x^{2} - x y=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- x)}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{- x^{2}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - x y=- x^{2}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- x$ and $Q(x)=- x^{2}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y - x^{2} y=- x y^{2}\,.
$$

Assume $y\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y - x^{2} y=- x y^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y - x^{2} y + x y^{2}=0 \\ y (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - x^{2} + x y)=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - x^{2} + x y=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(x)}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{x^{2}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + x y=x^{2}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=x$ and $Q(x)=x^{2}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{x + y}{x}\,.
$$

Assume $x\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

where $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ do not depend on $y.$

We have

$$
\begin{gathered}\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{x + y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=x^{2}\left(\frac{x + y}{x}\right) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=x (x + y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=x^{2} + x y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- x)}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{x^{2}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - x y=x^{2}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- x$ and $Q(x)=x^{2}.$

$$
\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{- x - y}{x}\,.
$$

Assume $x\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,

where $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ do not depend on $y.$

We have

$$
\begin{gathered}\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{- x - y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=x^{2}\left(\frac{- x - y}{x}\right) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=x (- x - y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=- x^{2} - x y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(x)}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{- x^{2}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + x y=- x^{2}\end{gathered}

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
- \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y e^{- x} + 5 y^{2}=y\,.
$$

Assume $y\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

where $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ do not depend on $y.$

We have

$$
\begin{gathered}- \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y e^{- x} + 5 y^{2}=y \\ - \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y e^{- x} + 5 y^{2} - y=0 \\ - y (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} e^{- x} - 5 y + 1)=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} e^{- x} - 5 y + 1=0 \\ e^{x}\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} e^{- x} - 5 y + 1\right)=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 5 y e^{x} + e^{x}=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- 5 e^{x})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{- e^{x}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 5 y e^{x}=- e^{x}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- 5 e^{x}$ and $Q(x)=- e^{x}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
- \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y e^{- x} - 2 y^{2}=- y\,.
$$

Assume $y\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

where $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ do not depend on $y.$

$$
\begin{gathered}- \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y e^{- x} - 2 y^{2}=- y \\ - \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y e^{- x} - 2 y^{2} + y=0 \\ - y (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} e^{- x} + 2 y - 1)=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} e^{- x} + 2 y - 1=0 \\ e^{x}\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} e^{- x} + 2 y - 1\right)=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 2 y e^{x} - e^{x}=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(2 e^{x})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{e^{x}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 2 y e^{x}=e^{x}\end{gathered}

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
7 x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+6 x y-3 x=4+3 y\,.
$$

Assume $x\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}7 x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+6 x y-3 x=4+3 y \\ 7 x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+(6 x-3)y=4+3 x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(\frac{6 x - 3}{7 x})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{\frac{3 x + 4}{7 x}}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=\frac{6 x - 3}{7 x}$ and $Q(x)=\frac{3 x + 4}{7 x}.$

knowledge_point.title: Writing First-Order Linear ODEs in Standard Form

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4{y}^{2}(\cos{(4 x )})^{2}=(6-(2)y\cos{(4 x )})^{2}\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\small \begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4{y}^{2}(\cos{(4 x )})^{2}=(6-(2)y\cos{(4 x )})^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4{y}^{2}(\cos{(4 x )})^{2}=36+4{y}^{2}(\cos{(4 x )})^{2}-24 y \cos{(4 x )} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=36-24 y \cos{(4 x )} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(24 \cos{(4 x )})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{36}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=24 \cos{(4 x )}$ and $Q(x)=36.$
